what_happened: In job c2h3, Athena's first reading of a request to build the records-history work covered too much for one producer run. The reading included the six record types (landing-intent, landing, intervention, checkpoint, legacy-exempt, import-manifest) with their schemas and validation, and also the writer and the host-rules check. The user corrected it before work began. They narrowed the job to the six record types in athena-data, with schemas, validation, round-trip and rejection tests, a CHANGELOG entry and doc comments citing the design. The writer and the host-rules check become two later jobs.
cause: Athena builds a reading from the request and its design source as one outcome. Nothing makes it compare the reading's size with what one producer run can finish before its fixed deadline. Nothing makes it split a multi-part design (types, writer, check) into separate jobs along natural seams. The class has recurred on three jobs, and each time only the user's correction applied the size bound. The existing cases show the reading stage does not learn from earlier corrections.
prevention: Add a size gate at the reading stage. Before a reading is accepted, count its separable deliverables (for example distinct components, record types plus a writer plus a check) and its estimated files. If the count is over a configured limit, the reading must split into one job per component and queue the rest as follow-up requests. The reading prompt must also say that a request naming several independent components yields one job for the first component and a named follow-up for each of the others. This gate would have kept the writer and the host-rules check out of this reading.
proposed_request: In athena-data, add schemas and validation for the six records-history record types: landing-intent, landing, intervention, checkpoint, legacy-exempt and import-manifest. Cite the design in doc comments. Add round-trip tests (write, read back, equal) and rejection tests (malformed or incomplete records are refused with a clear error) for each type. Add a CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry. Do not build the records writer or the host-rules check. They are separate later jobs.
